experiment_design.technical_details: This study proposes to validate the applicability of Nested Partially-Latent Class Models (npLCMs) for estimating etiological fractions in Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) case-control studies. Based on EV-Q020-2ce475b12c2a97ed8512e37a, npLCMs integrate multiple imperfect diagnostic measurements and covariates to estimate latent disease etiology probabilities. The technical implementation involves: 1) Defining a latent class structure representing potential etiological subtypes (e.g., genetic, environmental, idiopathic) without assuming prior biological truth; 2) Modeling the conditional probability of observed biomarkers/clinical indicators given latent classes, accounting for measurement error; 3) Incorporating explanatory variables (covariates) via a regression framework on the latent class probabilities (etiology regression); 4) Using Bayesian inference with MCMC or variational inference to estimate posterior distributions of etiological fractions. The key technical challenge is ensuring model identifiability given the high heterogeneity of ASD and the lack of gold-standard biomarkers, which will be addressed through sensitivity analyses on prior specifications and constraint structures.

The simulation will mimic the structure described in EV-Q020-2ce475b12c2a97ed8512e37a: multiple binary/continuous diagnostic indicators with known sensitivity/specificity profiles, and covariates (e.g., age, sex, prenatal exposure proxies).
datasets.target: Estimated Etiological Fractions (PEFs) for defined latent classes, along with their 95% credible intervals. Secondary target: Model convergence diagnostics (R-hat statistics, effective sample size) and parameter recovery accuracy against ground-truth simulation parameters.

experiment_design.methods: 1. **Model Specification**: Implement npLCM as described in EV-Q020-2ce475b12c2a97ed8512e37a. Let $Y_i$ be the vector of observed measurements for subject $i$, $Z_i$ be the latent etiology class, and $X_i$ be covariates. Model $P(Z_i|X_i)$ using a multinomial logistic regression and $P(Y_i|Z_i)$ using class-specific measurement models (e.g., Bernoulli for binary tests, Gaussian for continuous biomarkers). 2. **Inference**: Use Stan or PyMC3 for Bayesian estimation. 3. **Comparison Baseline**: Standard Multinomial Logistic Regression treating observed composite diagnosis as ground truth (ignoring measurement error). 4. **Validation**: Posterior predictive checks to assess model fit.

baselines: Standard Multinomial Logistic Regression (ignoring latent structure and measurement error)

metrics: Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of estimated etiological fractions vs. true simulation parameters
Coverage Probability of 95% Credible Intervals (proportion of times true parameter falls within CI)
Widest Confidence Interval Width (to assess precision gain over baselines)
Model Convergence Rate (percentage of chains converging with R-hat < 1.01)
experiments.ablation: 1. Varying the number of latent classes (K=2, 3, 4) to test robustness to model misspecification. 2. Removing covariates from the etiology regression component to assess the value of explanatory variable integration. 3. Varying measurement error rates (sensitivity/specificity) to test model resilience to noisy data.
experiments.validation_protocol: Split simulated data into 80% training and 20% testing. Perform 5-fold cross-validation on hyperparameters (e.g., prior variance). Evaluate metrics on the held-out test set. Conduct a simulation study with N=1000 replications to assess average performance.
